title: the plugin pipeline costs at most 2x plain per task
description: Implements the cost design in docs/research/pipeline-cost-design.md, section 6, on the user's decisions of 2026-10-07: G1 (the per-task intent review, the red-first grade and the inherited-test question move into the phase review, with a deferred close and a sign-off refusal), the phase-overhead budget raised to 1.00, and the main loop's cache TTL documented but not changed. The order is fixed by the user: implement, run each task's micro-test, and only then one single-task paid probe and the full benchmark, both run by the orchestrator. Each task's design section gives its mechanism, targets and micro-test; the task text below names what it owns.
desiredOutcome: a task run through the plugin pipeline costs at most 2x plain Claude Code doing the same task, measured like for like, with the phase overhead within 1.00 USD-equivalent a phase, each fix confirmed by its offline micro-test before any paid session

findings.issue: close-phase checks the landing property against the plan copy it was handed (`phase` loaded from `args.manifest`). It does not check the copy the merge brings in. Sign-off and task closes are committed on the phase branch. The parent's copy still shows the phase as it was at the fork: tasks pending, no `commit`. `phase_as_landed` already says this, and `gate_answer` already reads the branch tip for that reason. Against the parent's copy, `landing_refusals` finds no task with a commit and returns nothing. Concrete sequence under the default `phase`: 1) tasks are closed `deferred` on `audit/pN`; 2) `drive-phase next PN --answer sign-off` records the phase gate green, and then signoff refuses because tasks are owed answers; 3) from the parent checkout, run `close-phase.py docs/audit/audit-plan.json PN --project .`, adding `--branch audit/pN` if the composed name does not resolve. The gate is read at the tip and is green; `--override-verdict` also works, and it overrides only the gate. The review property is read from the parent's copy, so it is empty, and the branch merges with every task's answers missing. This repo is in that state now: `git show main:docs/audit/phases/P118.json` shows P118's tasks `pending` with commit null. Every `ra*` case in test_close_phase.py (:965-1062) runs close-phase with the branch checked out, so this path is never tested. The README row at :690 and COMPATIBILITY.md ('close-phase.py asks the same of the plan's record') both claim this refusal.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.13-v7t (685875a9): In `main`, when `landing_due` is true, run `review_answers_refusal` against the branch tip's copy (`landed` from `phase_as_landed`) as well as the handed copy, and refuse if either fails. When the tip's copy cannot be read, refuse rather than fall back to the handed copy. Add an `ra8` case: main checked out holding the pre-merge plan (task pending, no commit), the branch tip carrying a `deferred` task. `close-phase <main's manifest> P1 --project <main tree>` must exit 1 and must not merge.

findings.issue: Under `phase` (now the default), a phase reviewer's per-task `diverges`, `cannot-tell` or red-first `not-proved` never reaches a decision before the merge. Under `always`, `close_task` stops on these through `review_items`, as a `decide review-answer` human action item. Under `phase`: `triage()` reads only the filed return's `findings` and `verdict`; `render_triage` prints only open findings; `_carry_answers` writes any non-`deferred` word onto `intentCheck`, and `landing_problem` accepts it. The reviewer prompt says intent is not a finding and must not be filed as one, and `clean` beside `diverges` is a legitimate return. So the triage prints 'the phase review returned `clean`; no finding open'. `--answer sign-off` then runs the gate, sign-off, the commit and the merge in one step. The signoff output listing the carried answers is discarded on success (`run_signoff`). A task the reviewer said does not do what it asked lands without anyone deciding. The phase-level `intent.answer` against `desiredOutcome` is not shown either. The design (5.2: 'a `diverges` or a `not-proved` reaches a human at sign-off'; 5.4: 'acted on before the merge … the triage decision') and COMPATIBILITY's 'every answer … is still given; what moves is when' both rest on this.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.12-v7t (cdded1b5): In `triage`, read the filed phase return's `tasks` entries and its `intent`. List each `diverges` or `cannot-tell` answer, and each `not-proved` on a tdd task, as a triage line beside the findings. Do not offer `sign-off` until each line is answered, with a reason that goes into the summary. That is the same set `review_items` raises under `always`. Pin it with a drive case: a phase return whose `tasks` entry answers `diverges` with `findings: []` must stop at a decision naming that task, plus an allow twin where every entry answers `matches`.

findings.issue: A recorded fix task (`add --fixes`) closed with plain `done <fix> --commit <sha>` and no `--intent` records `deferred`, as the design and CHANGELOG allow ('with no `--intent` it records `deferred` like any task'). From there the phase cannot sign off: `landing_problem` refuses it because `deferred` is not an answer and the fix-task exception applies only to `not-asked`. `owed_answer` excludes fix tasks, so the phase brief does not list it and `review_due` does not dispatch for it. `phase_return_problems` refuses any entry for it ('owed no answer … or it is a recorded fix task'). Both the `done` line ('the phase review answers it, and sign-off refuses until it does') and the sign-off refusal ('Brief the phase reviewer … file its return') point to a remedy the filing verb refuses. The only way out is reopen → start → `done --intent not-asked`. The driver avoids this by always passing not-asked, so only the documented manual close reaches it.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.13-v7t (685875a9): Pick one rule and pin it with a case. Either `done` refuses a recorded fix task's close under `phase` without `--intent not-asked --intent-basis`, naming that remedy. Or `owed_answer` (and with it the brief, the filing check and `review_due`) treats a fix task whose `intentCheck` reads `deferred` as owed, like any task.

findings.issue: The shipped docs claim the landing property is wider than it is, and the 'followed, not enforced' half from design 5.2 reaches no shipped surface. The README row says 'sign-off and `close-phase.py` refuse while one lacks its answers'. The code asks this only of tasks that currently record a commit, and only when close-phase is the merge. Ways past it that are named only in docs/research: (a) work a task committed and then stopped recording. Example: `done P1.1 --commit C` (`deferred`) → `reopen P1.1 --reason x` → `cancel P1.1 --reason y` (or `move`, or restart and `done --no-change`) → `signoff P1 --verdict skipped` passes and close-phase merges C. The driver offers the same through its own `decide no-change` → `--answer no-change` when the executor has already committed. `repair-commits --apply` is another route. (b) Any caller can file the phase return: `--role` and `--head` are the caller's word. (c) A filed return can be rewritten: `docs/audit/**` is exempt from the plan gate (require-plan.py:851-853), guard-edits keeps only the journal append-only, and a changed answer (diverges→matches) passes sign-off; hd19 covers only a removed field. (d) After a hand or PR merge, close-phase stamps `mergedAt` without asking, because `landing_due` is false. The README's followed table has no row for any of these, and verbs-in-full's 'What it cannot hold' names only the task id and the role.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.13-v7t (685875a9): Narrow the README row (and COMPATIBILITY's wording) to 'each task that records a commit, at close-phase's own merge'. Add a followed row listing (a)-(d), each with its post-hoc evidence. For (a), the evidence is the commits past `baseRef` that no task records, which group sign-off's accounting already computes (audit-task.py `group_plan`). Name (c) in verbs-in-full, or extend guard-edits' append-only rule to `<evidence>/returns/**`.

findings.issue: 'Set `"always"` to restore the previous behaviour exactly' (COMPATIBILITY) and 'To keep today's behaviour, set … always' (CHANGELOG) are both false against the last release. Under `always`, every `done --commit` with neither a filed reviewer return for the current start nor `--intent not-asked --intent-basis` now exits 2 (audit-task.py:4975-4999, P118.3). That includes a typed `--intent matches` and a close with no `--intent`, both of which the previous release accepted. `start`, `done` and `signoff` also now refuse an out-of-vocabulary `review.perTask`. COMPATIBILITY names the done refusal in a separate entry, which contradicts 'exactly'. The CHANGELOG [Unreleased] section names it nowhere. CHANGELOG also leaves out three other changes in this phase. Every verb's default stdout is now one success line, with `--verbose` for the old text; this repo's own tools/check-git-pipeline.py g15 had to add `--verbose`. Stamp `compare` no longer goes stale when only recorders wrote (P118.11), which loosens a check. `file-return`, `done --from-return`, `brief`, `add --from-file` and `doctor --transcript` are new.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.13-v7t (685875a9): Change both sentences to say that `always` restores a reviewer per task, and that closes stay held to the filed-return rule (cite the COMPATIBILITY entry). Add CHANGELOG 'Changed' entries for the `done --commit` refusal, the one-line success output with `--verbose`, and the stamp's recorder exclusion. Add 'Added' entries for the new verbs.

findings.issue: Once `state.phaseReview.head` is set, `triage` never asks `review_due` again. A non-fix task added after that closes `deferred`, and the next `--answer sign-off` is refused by the signoff verb with no redispatch offered. Such tasks include the one the red-gate stop's own remedy creates (`audit-task.py add … --failing-from`, which has no `--fixes`). The model then has to brief and dispatch the phase reviewer outside the driver. The guarantee holds; only the driver's path to completing sign-off breaks.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.12-v7t (cdded1b5): In `triage`, when a head is marked but `review_due()` still names a task owed its answers, drop the mark and dispatch a fresh phase review at the current head. Add a drive case: red phase gate → added task → sign-off reaches a new phase-review dispatch.

findings.issue: `_commit_stamp` runs `commit-audit-state.py` in the parent's checkout. It stages the phase's manifest file (in single-file layout, the whole plan), the journal directory and the evidence directory as they stand. Another session's uncommitted plan or journal changes in a shared parent checkout therefore go into a commit titled 'landed on <parent>'. This is the reverse of the sweep P118.8 set out to remove.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.13-v7t (685875a9): Before committing, have `commit_landing` compare the parent tree's plan and journal changes with the stamp fields and this run's own row. When anything else is pending there, report it as `landingCommitSkipped` and leave it for that tree's own work, rather than committing it.

findings.issue: `done --no-change` records only the HEAD it examined. It never checks that the task's declared files are unchanged since its start, so a close with no commit is the caller's word. Under G1 the landing property now depends on this: a task with no commit is never asked.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.13-v7t (685875a9): Refuse `--no-change` when `git diff <phase.baseRef or the start's HEAD>..HEAD -- <task files>` is non-empty, or when the tree has uncommitted changes to those files. Otherwise record the diff stat beside `examinedAt`.

findings.issue: Under the new default review.perTask=phase, the phase review's per-task answers are recorded but never shown to anyone. This covers `diverges`, `cannot-tell`, red-first `not-proved`, and a phase-level intent `diverges`. The triage reads only `verdict` and the open findings. review_items, which raises the `decide review-answer` human action item, runs only on a per-task reviewer's return. Reproduced on a scratch fixture: the phase review filed P1.2 with answer=diverges and redFirst=not-proved. The triage printed `the phase review returned clean; no finding open`, then sign-off and the merge ran with no human prompt. landing_problem (_filed_returns.py:263-296) accepts `diverges` as an answer. The design (pipeline-cost-design.md:1631 and the table at :2345) says these answers reach a human at sign-off and are acted on before the merge. Under `always` the same answers stop the drive.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.12-v7t (cdded1b5): In triage(), read the filed phase return's `tasks` entries and the phase `intent`. List each diverges, cannot-tell, not-proved or flagged entry as a triage line. Make sign-off over them a human decision that needs --reason, the same way invariant-breach is handled. Add a drive case where a diverges entry blocks a silent sign-off, shown red against today's triage.

findings.issue: `/audit:phase <id> --confirm-high-risk` still records a risk.confirmed row, and phase.md says only tasks not on the covered list stop and ask. The driver never reads that row. Reproduced: with P1.1 covered by the row, the drive still printed `decide high-risk P1.1 ... Ask the human (AskUserQuestion)`. The unattended run the flag exists for now stalls at the first high-risk commit. At base this was supported (execute-task.md:458-476).
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.12-v7t (cdded1b5): Before deciding high-risk, ask record-risk-confirmation's covered set (or the journal's risk.confirmed rows for this phase). Mark covered tasks confirmed and print `high-risk confirmed in advance` in the did-line. Add a drive case for a covered task and one for a task that is not covered.

findings.issue: The `meta.runtimeBoot` sign-off step is gone. At base it was phase-signoff.md step 4: cold-boot the app, and stop with a human action item when the runtime is unreachable. The driver runs gate, invariants, signoff, commit and land with no boot check. No command body reads phase-signoff.md any more, and nothing in STEPS states the rule. review.md's description and the README row still promise an `optional runtime boot`. T2 required every rule to be re-homed and none dropped.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.12-v7t (cdded1b5): When meta.runtimeBoot is set and the phase touched appRootPath, add a step before the verdict that prints a `decide runtime-boot` (a human answer: booted / not-reachable + reason). Or drop the claim from review.md, the README and CHANGELOG as a recorded decision.

findings.issue: The driver reads only the gate's exit code. run-test-gate prints `NO OVERLAP WITH THIS WORK ... Decide whether this gate can grade this work before signing it off.` and `TREE CHANGED OUTSIDE THIS WORK` on a green exit. The driver turns both into `gate P1.1 green` and goes on to commit, close and sign off. Reproduced with a gate that prints only tests/unrelated_test.py: the banner appeared under --verbose, and the default print said `gate P1.1 green; ... closed P1.1`. That decision, which the base orchestrator was told to make, is now skipped with no record.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.12-v7t (cdded1b5): Capture those banner lines from the gate's output and carry a bounded clause into the did-line, for example `gate P1.1 green (NO OVERLAP)`. For the phase gate, turn it into a decision before the verdict. Carry the clause into the phase reviewer's per-task brief entry too.

findings.issue: When close-phase exits 3 (the parent moved), the driver offers one option, `no-ff`, and prints an empty rule. The model therefore answers alone and lands a merge commit. Base phase-signoff made this a human's call (AskUserQuestion: --no-ff recommended, or stop and leave it unmerged; never rebase). The `leave unmerged` option and the never-rebase rule are both gone.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.12-v7t (cdded1b5): Give not-fast-forward the options (`no-ff`, `leave`), with `leave` needing --reason. Add the rule line `ask the human; never rebase - it rewrites the task commit SHAs`. Add a drive case.

findings.issue: There is no way past a blocked task. stop-blocked tells the model to run `audit-task.py start <id>`. For the usual block (attempts exhausted, the path decide gate-red prescribes), start refuses, and `start --force --reason` refuses too. Both reproduced: exit 2, `would spend one past the ceiling`. The `stopped` rule forbids a hand edit, and base /audit:run offered a confirmed reset of attempts. In a phase drive, a blocked task gives `decide stalled P1: no task is ready - P1.1 blocked; P1.2 pending on P1.1` with no answer line and no rule. The command bodies say to answer with a printed option, and none is printed.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.12-v7t (cdded1b5): Add a verb that resets attempts after a human confirms (for example `audit-task.py unblock <id> --reason`, journaled), and name it in stop-blocked's rule. Give decide stalled a rule that names the blocked task's remedy, or turn it into a `stopped` print with that remedy.

findings.issue: A fix task's diff is never reviewed. Base sign-off looped until clean. Reproduced: a finding led to `--answer fix`, the fix task closed, and the triage was re-printed from the old head's return as `no finding open`. The phase then signed off. The fix task is closed `not-asked` with the basis `the phase review that raised the finding is its review`, but that review predates the fix. /audit:review cannot ask for a re-review either: once the drive state holds a head, `redispatch` exists only for no-phase-review-return.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.12-v7t (cdded1b5): When fix tasks closed after the recorded head, print a decision offering `re-review` (dispatch the phase review at the new head, scoped to the fix commits) or `sign-off` with --reason. Reword the fix-task basis to say the fix itself was not reviewed.

findings.issue: In a driver session, step 3 of the benchmark is misread. A fix task added by `--answer fix` runs inside the driver's subprocess, so no main-loop planning verb is seen. Landing and lock release also happen inside the driver, so `lands`/`releases` never fire. Reproduced with stream-cost's own _fx_driven over the driver's real prints: with a fix task, requests 1-10 (the phase review's dispatch, the triage, the fix task) were all `cycle`, P1.3 counted as a cycle task, and sign-off was the last request only. There were no `fix task` or `close` spans. The per-task ratio (cycle cost / 0.459507) is inflated and the phase overhead deflated whenever a fix task runs. The single-task probe (step 2) is readable: its cycle is 3 requests.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.12-v7t (cdded1b5): Have the driver print stable did-words, as constants beside STARTED/CLOSED, for `fix task <id> added`, `signed off`, `landed` and the lock release. Have request_marks read them as adds/lands/releases. Add an sp case over a driven sign-off with a fix task, red against today's find_spans.

findings.issue: The one-line success output also drops what the write itself decided. Reproduced: `add --from-file` printed `phase P2 added with P2.1 -- two`. Its --verbose form says `gate: none (the manifest declares no meta.buildCommands)`, an EMPTY gate that base phase.md required printing because sign-off then rests on review alone. A single add also hides the derived-gate basis and the `ready now -- /audit:run <id>` line. task.md still says the output names the journal row and the next command.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.13-v7t (685875a9): Keep the `gate:` basis line, and any WARNING naming an id this write touched, in the success line or beside it. Drop only the re-printed warnings that predate the write. Fix task.md's sentence.

findings.issue: The documented batch shape for `/audit:phase add` is phase {title, desiredOutcome, description}. The argument-hint still advertises --gate, --gate-clear, --blocked-by, --area, --review-skill and --id. A model writing the documented shape drops them silently, although BATCH_PHASE_KEYS accepts testGate, blockedBy, area, reviewSkill and id. `--park` is routed only for a phase branch. The batch refuses an empty `tasks`, so adding an empty phase to fill later, which add-phase allowed, is no longer reachable from this body.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.14-v7t (7b5be34e): List the optional phase keys in the shape and map each hint flag to its key, with `--gate-clear` written as testGate []. Route `--park`, and a phase with no tasks yet, to `add-phase` explicitly.

findings.issue: `/audit:phase` no longer runs a wave in parallel. next_task drives one task at a time. The command description (`parallel where safe`) and the README row (`parallel where files are disjoint`) still promise parallel runs, and CHANGELOG does not mention the change. A wide phase's wall clock now grows with its task count, and nothing tells the user.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.12-v7t (cdded1b5): Record the serial choice and its reason in CHANGELOG and correct the description and README row. Alternatively, dispatch a wave's executors together and run the gates serially once all have filed.

findings.issue: The `--dry-run` preview now runs only close-phase --dry-run and resolve-branch. It no longer lists the ready tasks the run would execute, which the base preview printed. For a phase not yet started, close-phase --dry-run exits 1 (`no branch is recorded ... Pass --branch`), reproduced on a fixture. The common preview therefore shows a refusal and a branch line.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.14-v7t (7b5be34e): Add `audit-status.py --short --phase <id>` (or the driver's read-only `next --dry-run`) to step 0. Treat close-phase's no-branch exit as `not started yet` instead of relaying it.

findings.issue: Every pipeline body still says `see reference/manifest-conventions.md` (36 KB), review.md ends with a phase-signoff.md pointer, and the ADO echo step says `as reference/tracker-sync.md says` (19 KB). first_reads only matches a `Read ... first` paragraph, so the ceiling gate cannot see these reference reads. The rule they point at is already stated inline.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.14-v7t (7b5be34e): Drop the `see reference/...` clauses where the rule is inline. Put the echo's few hard rules into the ado-echo step text. Widen the gate to flag a `reference/` path in a pipeline body or a STEPS rule.

findings.issue: The TTL row has three defects. (a) It counts `isSidechain: true` entries as main-loop requests. On a synthetic transcript, two sidechain entries cut the real 690 s main-loop gap to a reported 300 s and added their writes. (b) The `would cost $X at a five-minute TTL` figure prices the same tokens without the re-writes the gap implies, so it reads cheaper exactly when it would not be. (c) A gap of exactly 300 s is called one that `exceeds five minutes`. The row is reachable through doctor.md's $ARGUMENTS and is not loaded by the pipeline.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.14-v7t (7b5be34e): Skip isSidechain entries. Say the five-minute figure excludes the re-writes, or omit it when a gap is at least 300 s. Use `reaches` or `>` wording consistently.

findings.issue: Both briefs say to write the return `to a file` and pipe `< <your return file>`, with no location given. The reviewer has no Write tool and its prompt forbids anything that writes. The plan gate refuses an executor's in-project write outside its task files. Each wrong guess costs agent requests.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.14-v7t (7b5be34e): Print a heredoc form of the submit command, or name an exempt path under stateDir beside the brief.

findings.issue: The one verb the main loop runs on every /audit:resume is not wired to the success line. It printed 434 bytes over six lines on a fixture.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.14-v7t (7b5be34e): Route its __main__ through _output.terse_cli with a summarizer that keeps the commit SHA and any `degraded:` line.

findings.issue: Two stale or unreadable texts reach users. The triage prices a fix task on `pipeline-cost design 5.4`, a document a plugin install does not ship. verbs-in-full.md, which the guide reads, keeps procedures the driver no longer follows: `Offer a confirmed reset of attempts to 0`, `Proceed only if the human explicitly confirms re-execution`, and dry-run `parallel groups`.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.14-v7t (7b5be34e): Name a basis the user can open, or say `a benchmark prediction, not this project`. Mark or rewrite the stale guard and dry-run paragraphs to match what the driver does.

findings.issue: No verb resets `attempts` on an exhausted task. Base /audit:run told the orchestrator to reset it, which could only be a hand edit.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.13-v7t (685875a9): This is the verb finding 6 asks for.

findings.issue: The R1 fix is incomplete: the last task's close is never at the branch tip. `close_task` runs commit-task-work first. That commit stages the shard as it stands, with the task still in_progress and `commit` null. Only after that does `done` write the close (`deferred`, commit C). Nothing commits the plan again until `commit_signoff`. So the phase-review and triage window has a gap, and so does any refused or red sign-off. In that window the tip copy shows the last task with no commit, and the parent's copy shows it pending. Bypass in a worktree layout under the default key: from the parent's checkout, run `close-phase.py <parent manifest> PN --project . [--branch audit/pN]`. Neither copy has a task to ask about, so C merges with no answers. For a one-task phase, that is the whole phase. The gate check does not stop this. `gate_answer` reads the ledger through `branch_texts` (:1666-1686), which also reads the worktree's uncommitted evidence. So a phase gate recorded in the worktree reads green without `--override-verdict`, and `--override-verdict` covers the remaining case. ra8 and ra9 commit the deferred close on the branch, which the driver never does for the last task. README:691 and COMPATIBILITY.md:355-360 say close-phase refuses while 'a task that records a commit' lacks its answers. Here the only copy that records the commit is the one close-phase does not read.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.15-v7t (487cedd3): 1) When any task's key reads `phase`, refuse a landing whose tip copy records no sign-off verdict (`_mio.signoff_recorded(landed)`). Only `commit_signoff` puts the last close at the tip, and this rule still holds after the worktree is removed. 2) Also ask the property of the worktree's on-disk plan when the branch is checked out there (`_phase_project(git_root, project, observation['phaseTree'])`), the same way `branch_texts` reads the ledger. 3) Add case ra12: a worktree holds audit/p1 and its only task is closed `deferred` at C, with the plan change uncommitted as the driver leaves it, and a green phase-gate row sits in the worktree. close-phase run from main must exit 1, and C must not be in main. Add an allow twin after the sign-off is committed. 4) Bring the README:691 and COMPATIBILITY wording into line.

findings.issue: The rule that a human settles a reviewer's `diverges`, `cannot-tell`, `not-proved` or `flagged` (R2/R9) is enforced only inside the driver's triage. The documented `/audit:phase signoff <id> --verdict passed --summary x` runs `audit-task.py signoff`. `_carry_answers` copies those answers onto `intentCheck` and signs off, because `landing_problem` accepts any answer except `deferred`. The next `drive-phase.py next <id>` sees `signed_off(phase)` and goes straight to `finish_signoff`, then close-phase. The triage is never built, and close-phase accepts the same answers. So, through one documented verb, a task the phase reviewer said does not do what it asked lands with no human asked. The same route also skips the new runtime-boot and gate-coverage decisions. No followed-table row names this route: row 397 covers order only and row 402 covers whether answers exist. CHANGELOG:82 says the answers reach a human 'before the landing'.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.15-v7t (487cedd3): Enforce it in the verb. Move the human-answer predicate (`human_answers`' words) into `_filed_returns`, so the driver and the verb share one definition. In `_carry_answers`, under a `phase` key, refuse while a filed phase return holds such an answer, unless `--accept-answers "<the human's words>"` is passed. Record those words in the summary and in the `phase.verdict` row. Have the driver pass its accepted reasons through that flag. Pin it: sign-off over a `diverges` entry exits 2, and the same with `--accept-answers` signs off. If the verb is meant to stay 'followed' only, add a README followed row that names this route and the evidence it leaves: a filed `diverges` beside a signed-off phase.

findings.issue: When the tip holds no copy of the plan, `landed_answers_refusal` refuses every landing that has a task keyed `phase`, and prints 'Commit the plan on <branch>'. A lost tip is not the only reason a tip has no copy. The plan may sit outside the git root, which README:1744-1747 supports ('Prefer keeping the manifest inside'), or be ignored or excluded. Such a plan is never in any commit, and the copy close-phase is handed is not a snapshot from the fork: it is the live record shared across branches. Under the default key, such a project can land no phase through close-phase or the driver, even with every answer bound, and the remedy it prints cannot be applied. ra10 pins this refusal on an excluded plan as if it were intended.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.15-v7t (487cedd3): Refuse on an unreadable tip only when the plan is versioned: inside the git root, not ignored, and tracked at the parent or at `baseRef`. Otherwise the handed copy (plus the worktree copy from finding 1, where one exists) is the record, and `review_answers_refusal` on it is the whole check. Add an allow case: an excluded plan whose task has a commit with answers bound, landed from the same checkout. Keep a refusal case for a tracked plan whose tip copy cannot be read.

findings.issue: Task `files` entries are relative to the project directory (README:1744: 'Task files stay project-dir-relative (e.g. test/src/foo.ts)'). `_no_change_moves` passes them unchanged as pathspecs to `git -C <project>/<gitRoot> log` and `status`. In the documented 'Git repo in a subdirectory' layout (gitRoot set), every pathspec then points at <gitRoot>/<gitRoot>/... and matches nothing. The refusal never fires, so a `--no-change` close over committed work passes, which is the route past the landing property that R8 meant to close. `commit-task-work.stage_targets` (:289-301) maps the same entries through `os.path.join(project, name)` and `_invariants._rel(abs, git_root)` for exactly this reason. The CHANGELOG and README claim this refusal without saying it depends on the layout.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.15-v7t (487cedd3): Map each entry the way `stage_targets` does: join it to the project, then make it relative to the git root, and name an entry that falls outside the root rather than dropping it. Do this before both git calls. Add an ncm case with gitRoot pointing at a subdirectory; it fails against the current code.

findings.issue: `fixes_after` lists every recorded fix task closed after the review head, whatever its key. Under `always` (and under `signals` where a signal fired), that fix task had its own per-task reviewer. Even so, the triage says 'their diff unreviewed', and sign-off writes 'Fix task(s) ... signed off with their diff unreviewed.' into the recorded summary, which is false. Separately, `human_answers` reads the phase-level intent under every key. So an `always` phase with a review skill now stops on a phase intent of `diverges` or `cannot-tell`, while CHANGELOG:82 says this happens 'Under review.perTask: phase' only.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.16-v7t (5b425cc2): Limit `fixes_after` to fix tasks whose `intentCheck` is the `not-asked` close the phase key writes. Make CHANGELOG/COMPATIBILITY say that the phase-intent stop applies under every key.

findings.issue: close-phase now prints R7's new `landingCommitSkipped` on a later line ('the stamp is not committed here: ...'). `land()` keeps only the first line, so the drive prints `landed (...)` and `done`. Meanwhile the parent's checkout holds an uncommitted `mergedAt` stamp, and nobody is told.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.16-v7t (5b425cc2): When close-phase's output contains 'not committed here', add a clause to the did-line, for example 'stamp left uncommitted in <tree>; re-run close-phase there once it is clean'.

findings.issue: Answering `accept` on gate-coverage goes back through `signoff_step` and `run_signoff`, which runs and records the whole phase gate a second time, because the first green run is not marked. Because `coverageAccepted` is set, the second run's banners are not read at all, so a banner that only the second run prints is accepted without the human seeing it. `coverageAccepted` and `bootConfirmed` also survive a later red gate followed by a fix task, so a fix that touches the app root is not boot-checked again.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.16-v7t (5b425cc2): Record the green phase-gate run (runId and head) in the drive state, and skip re-running the gate on `accept` while HEAD is unchanged. Clear `coverageAccepted` and `bootConfirmed` when a task closes after they were given.

findings.issue: `unblock` writes a new journal action from inside the verb, `task.unblock`. The journal action list and the 'written in process by `audit-task.py`' list both name `task.block` but not `task.unblock`.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.15-v7t (487cedd3): Add a `task.unblock` bullet (details: taskId, phaseId, reason, changes) and add the action to the in-process list.

findings.issue: The command description, which is the text the command picker shows, still says '(every ready task, parallel where safe, then sign-off)'. The driver runs one task at a time. The README and CHANGELOG were corrected, and R19's resolution explicitly named the description.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.16-v7t (5b425cc2): Change it to 'every ready task, one at a time in id order, then sign-off', and drop 'wave' from step 2.

findings.issue: Two of the new sign-off decisions only let a human say yes. `gate-coverage` offers only `accept`. `runtime-boot` offers `booted` or `not-reachable`, and `not-reachable` keeps the same decision pending. When the human says no (the gate grades nothing of this work, or the app boots and crashes), there is no way back to the work. A pending decision with no task is replayed on every `next`, whatever the plan now holds (`pending_still_applies` returns True). `/audit:run` of a task added as the remedy is also refused: 'this phase's drive waits on a gate-coverage decision'. Reproduced on fixtures: after `audit-task.py add` and `retarget --gate-set`, `next P1` re-printed `decide gate-coverage`, and `--answer decline` was refused. After `not-reachable` with a crash reason and an added fix task, `next P1` re-asked runtime-boot and `next P1.2-xic` was refused. The only way forward is a false `accept`/`booted`. That answer stays in the drive state (`coverageAccepted`/`bootConfirmed`) and switches off the same check on the tree after the fix. Reproduced: added P1.2-xic, then `accept --reason "the human: no - added P1.2-xic"`. The phase gate re-ran, signoff refused because the task was open, and the drive ran P1.2-xic. The final phase gate printed NO OVERLAP again and no decision fired. The recorded summary reads 'Gate banner accepted: the human: no - ...'. The triage's `[accept]` lines are the same class: a human who wants a diverging task fixed has only `accept`.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.16-v7t (5b425cc2): Give each of these decisions an answer that hands back to the work. For example, `decline --reason` on gate-coverage and runtime-boot, and on the triage's answers: it records the human's words, drops the pending decision and lets the drive run tasks added since. Clear `coverageAccepted`, `bootConfirmed` and `answersAccepted` when a task closes after they were given, or bind each to the HEAD it was given at, so the gate and boot after a fix are asked again. Apply the same to `breachAccepted` (invariant-breach, from P118.8, has the same shape). Add a drive case: banner, then decline, then a task added and driven, then the final gate asks gate-coverage again. Its twin is a plain accept that signs off.

findings.issue: `--answer accept` on gate-coverage goes back through `signoff_step` -> `run_signoff`, which runs the whole phase gate (and `derive-phase-gate.py`) a second time. That is a second evidence row and a second full suite's wall clock, for an answer about the first run. The fixture's did-line printed `phase gate green` again after the accept.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.16-v7t (5b425cc2): Keep the green run's runId and HEAD in the drive state. On an accept at an unchanged HEAD, go straight to the invariants and the verdict; the newest ledger row is still the run the verdict binds to.

findings.issue: Any `risk.confirmed` row ever written for the phase that names the task counts as confirmation, with no bound in time. A high-risk task that is reopened and re-run commits unattended on an answer given for an earlier commit. record-risk-confirmation.py's own contract says the list covers open work as it stood at the moment of the answer.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.16-v7t (5b425cc2): Only count a row written after the task's most recent `task.reopen` row (or after its last `completedAt` was cleared). Add an hr case: confirm, run, reopen, run again, and it must stop at `decide high-risk`.

findings.issue: `decide stalled` and `stop-blocked` name `audit-task.py unblock` for every blocked task. `unblock` refuses a task blocked with attempts left, which is the usual result of `--answer block` at the first red gate, at high-risk or at no-executor-return; it points to `start` instead. On the fixture, the stalled print listed 'P1.1 blocked; P1.2 blocked' (P1.2 at 1 of 3 attempts) under a single unblock rule, so each such task costs a refused call first.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.16-v7t (5b425cc2): Render the remedy per blocked task from attempts against maxAttempts: `unblock` when they are spent, `start` otherwise. Add a bk case for a task blocked at 1 of 3.

findings.issue: `git log --since=<startedAt>` includes a commit made in the same second. The driver starts the next task right after committing the previous one. On a fixture where P1.1 and P1.2 share src/f1.txt, a later `done P1.2 --no-change` was refused in 3 of 4 trials, blaming P1.1's commit made in the second P1.2 started. The remedy printed ('close it --commit <sha> naming the work, or put the files back') would bind the sibling's commit to the task or revert the sibling's work. Under the driver it is rarely reached, because a no-work task closes on a record-only commit.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.15-v7t (487cedd3): Bound the span below by the HEAD at the task's start (record it on start, or read it from the `task.start` row) rather than by committer date. findings.issue: Rule (c): a path that signed off at round 2 now loops. The green phase-gate run is reused whenever HEAD has not moved. But the sign-off verb also checks that the run was measured under the gate the phase declares now and over its files as they stand. Changing either without a commit makes the reused run stale. The verb then refuses every `sign-off` answer, and nothing in the driver clears `phaseGate`; only `decline` does, and the gate-coverage decision is not asked again because `coverageAccepted` holds at the same HEAD. Reproduced on a scratch fixture (per_task=phase, phase gate `echo tests/unrelated_test.py 1 passed`): drive to `decide gate-coverage`, run `audit-task.py retarget P1 --gate-set "echo src/f1.txt 1 passed"`, then `next P1 --answer accept --reason ...`. Result: exit 1, `phase gate green (reused 2026-10-08T08:26:54Z.90404a)`, and the verb refused with '...measured under the gate [echo tests/unrelated_test.py 1 passed] ... and the phase declares [echo src/f1.txt 1 passed] now'. Three more rounds of triage then `--answer sign-off` gave the same refusal, and the state still named the old run. An uncommitted edit to src/f1.txt between the gate and the accept gives the same loop ('scopeDigest was ... and is ... now'). At round 2, run_signoff ran the gate again and both sequences signed off. The way out is the printed `run-test-gate.py ... --record` run by hand. After it, sign-off passes but still reuses the OLD run's banner list ('reused ...29bd18'), while the verdict binds to the new run (...45ea38). So nobody saw the banners of the run the verdict stands on, and the summary's 'Gate banner accepted' describes the other run. This breaks the premise R36's resolution relied on ('the newest ledger row is still the run the verdict binds to') whenever the gate or the files move without a commit; the docstring admits the uncommitted-edit case but not that it loops.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.17-v7t (1dd702f2): Store the run's gate entries and scopeDigest in `phaseGate` alongside `head`. Reuse it only while all three still match, for example by asking `_verdict_binding.phase_binding` before reusing. Also pop `phaseGate` whenever anything after the gate refuses, the sign-off verb included, so the next sign-off measures again. Add a drive case: gate-coverage → `retarget --gate-set` → accept signs off on one fresh run whose banners were read. Its twin is dc4: accept at an unchanged gate and tree reuses the run.

findings.issue: Rule (a). Under `always` or `signals`, close-phase lands a phase that has no sign-off verdict, so an unsettled answer in a filed phase return lands with no human asked. Reproduced on a scratch fixture (per_task=always, meta.reviewSkill set): the phase review was filed with intent `diverges`, and the triage printed `phase intent diverges - ... [accept]`. Then `close-phase.py <plan> P1 --project <root>` exited 0 with `audit/p1-one -> main (no-checkout)`, `mergedAt` stamped and `review.status` None. The same sequence under `phase` exits 1. This diff widens the human stop to 'every review.perTask value' (README:691 'Under every value, sign-off ... refuses while a filed phase return holds a diverges, cannot-tell ...'; COMPATIBILITY: 'that stop on a phase intent holds under every review.perTask value'). The landing only asks for a verdict where a task's key reads `phase`. The gap predates this round: round 2 lands the same way. It is listed here because it sits in the function this diff rewrote and on the property this diff extended.
findings.resolution: fixed in P118.17-v7t (1dd702f2): In `landed_answers_refusal`, under every key: when a landing is due and `_fr.needs_human(_fr.phase_returns(...))` holds an answer, refuse unless the tip copy (or, for an unversioned plan, the on-disk copy) records a sign-off verdict. Only the verb writes that verdict, and the verb has already checked the settlement. Add a case: the sim above exits 1 and merges nothing. Its twin: the same phase lands once it is signed off with the answer settled, and an `always` phase whose returns hold no such answer lands as before. If this is out of scope, add a followed-table row naming the route and the evidence it leaves: a filed `diverges` beside `mergedAt` with no `review.status`.

findings.issue: The verb's refusal sends a hand-run sign-off to `drive-phase.py next <pid>`. When a review skill resolves and no drive state exists, the driver first dispatches a new phase review. Sim: after the refusal 'phase: intent cannot-tell ... run `drive-phase.py next P1` and answer its triage', `next P1` printed `dispatch audit:audit-reviewer P1`. That is a second paid review just to record one accept, and the old answer stays in the triage either way. Under the group door the remedy is printed per member. Answering that member's triage `sign-off` would sign off and land the member alone.

Or say in the refusal text that a review is dispatched, and, for a group, to answer only `accept` and sign the group off again.

outcome.technical:
Design T7. One success-line helper in _output.py (success_line, terse_choice and terse_cli, marked "the success line") decides what a verb prints. A non-zero exit prints everything unchanged. --verbose prints today's text byte-identical. --json and --help keep the long form. A verb whose output is a payload prints it whole.

Each verb the driver or the main loop calls is wired through it from its __main__, so in-process callers see today's text. The verbs are audit-task, run-test-gate, stamp-verification, commit-task-work, audit-lock, verify-invariants, close-phase, validate-manifest, audit-lookup and audit-status. Success lines measured on the fixtures are 48 to 197 bytes. stamp take and red keep their parsed payloads whole. audit-lookup answers and audit-status's entry view print whole, because callers fold or paste them. run-test-gate prints in full when its machine line is not exclusive.

check-git-pipeline g15 passes --verbose to read the long form.
